title: Emergency Communications between Parents and their Children given Smartphone Ban in Secondary Schools
what_it_is: Emergency Communications between Parents and their Children given Smartphone Ban in Secondary Schools

sections.label: MOE support for school smartphone guidelines
sections.summary: MOE engaged school leaders and provided implementation guidelines, FAQs and shared good practices to support secondary schools in implementing tightened smartphone and smartwatch guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: To support secondary schools in implementing the tightened guidelines for use of smartphones and smartwatches, the Ministry of Education (MOE) had engaged school leaders and provided resources such as implementation guidelines, answers to Frequently Asked Questions, and we have also shared good practices by schools that have seen positive outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: On enforcement, MOE provides schools with guidelines to formulate their discipline policies and school rules based on their student profile and student needs.

sections.label: Emergency communication protocols for parents
sections.summary: Schools have emergency communication protocols; parents can contact the general office, students can use general office phones, and students need not own a handphone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Schools also have protocols for emergency communication with parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Should parents have an urgent message to relay to their children, they can contact the school's general office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Students who need to contact their parents may also do so using phones in the general office.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: There is no need for students to own or use a handphone.

sections.label: Parental support for the ban
sections.summary: Parents are largely supportive of the ban, some have questions about implementation, and MOE continues to engage schools and school leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: By and large, parents are supportive of the ban.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Some continue to have questions about how it ought to be done and how it ought to be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: And MOE continues to engage the schools and the school leaders on how best to do it.
